newsitem.title: CANADA: RTRS - Placer plans no more big shifts in hedging.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Placer plans no more big shifts in hedging.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc, which liquidated hedges on 1.7 million ounces of gold earlier this year in a major policy shift, said Friday it anticipated no more big changes in its forward sales.
"We don't see any significant changes in our hedging," Placer chief financial officer Ian Austin said in an interview at a mining conference.

The gold company now has forward sales covering about 3.6 million ounces of gold, he said. That is down from a hedge position of 5.5 million ounces before the liquidation and 3.8 million ounces when the move was announced in May.
The current amount sold forward represented less than two years of Placer's production and about 15 percent of its reserves, Austin said.

In a move closely watched by metals traders, Placer said in May that it was closing out hedges on 1.7 million ounces of gold that would have required it to deliver at prices of US$450 an ounce or less. It took the step to increase its exposure to fluctuations in the gold price.
Austin said Placer pegged its hedging more to production levels than reserves and would seek to hedge not more than half of any year's production.
Currently the company had 30 to 40 percent of annual production hedged for the next four to five years, he said.
Placer's hedge program has been profitable. It has US$400 million in gains from hedging since 1987 and the unrealized gain on its hedges now stands at about US$200 million.
"This is a very significant earnings impact even for a company of our size," Austin said.

While historical analysis showed producers could maximize profits by hedging a high proportion of their output, many investors, especially investment funds, opposed that strategy because it reduced exposure to the gold price, he said.
